transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (NexusHead ML), Sara Lee (Infra), Kevin O'Malley (Security), Aisha Khan (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Quick check-in on pilot onboarding. Some network bits pending, few perf results shared, plan for deeper benchmark next week.

00:00 Laura Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i see we have the usual folks on, uh quick check — did everyone get the invite and the test accounts?
00:08 Tom Reynolds: yeah got the invite, i logged in this morning, there was one issue with the service account role, Sara is looking into it
00:15 Sara Lee: yeah i spoke to infra, it's a IAM role mismatch, should be quick to fix, we've re-run the provisioning but, um, just need to confirm the service principal is in the right group
00:30 Miguel Santos: cool, while we're on access, i pushed the small sample dataset into the test bucket, you should see the sample prompts and the tokenized examples, tom can you confirm?
00:42 Tom Reynolds: yeah i can see it, um one thing, the sample has some long context sequences that matched our real traffic, which was helpful
00:55 Laura Kim: perfect, thanks. quick recap from our side: we ran a baseline bench on hosted tier, 3 runs, 1k concurrent simulated rps bursts, p50 about 120ms, p95 around 480ms for the default model, we think there's room to tune with KV cache and batching
01:20 Kevin O'Malley: sorry can i jump in — those numbers are for hosted right? we are still evaluating private/dedicated for compliance reasons, yes?
01:32 Laura Kim: correct, this was hosted perf. we included a dedicated projection in the doc but we haven't run the dedicated cluster yet. Miguel, maybe say more on tuning?
01:40 Miguel Santos: yeah so what we saw was that when the context lengths increase above ~1k tokens the KV cash, sorry KV cache, grows and cold-starts hit p95. there's two levers: increase prefix cache TTL and enable continuous batching for smaller tail latency. Also quantization profile can reduce throughput CPU on the host if you go dedicated, but that needs validation
02:05 Tom Reynolds: when you say continuous batching, is that something we toggle per-route? we have some real-time endpoints that can't tolerate 200ms batching windows
02:17 Miguel Santos: right, it's per-endpoint. we can set max latency per-batch to 15ms for the realtime route and larger for async routes. the trade-off is cost per token vs lit — latency sorry
02:30 Aisha Khan: just to clarify for the timeline — we need SSO+SAML in place before we go into security review, is that still on track?
02:40 Priya Patel: yes, Laura and i confirmed SSO setup tasks; we have the SAML metadata from nexus, pr iya, uh, we've already started configuring in the console. should be finished by EOD friday, unless there are firewall blocks
02:55 Kevin O'Malley: firewall's the other thing — we need clear outbound CIDR and port ranges. also KMS keys: who's going to hold root KMS for the private deployment? our compliance wants customer-owned keys
03:12 Laura Kim: noted. we support customer-managed KMS for private. Miguel will send the integration notes. Kevin can you send the KMS owner contact?
03:21 Kevin O'Malley: yeah i'll email the security mailbox, expect details by friday
03:30 Miguel Santos: on the perf bench, i want to call out one caveat — the initial run used the default model with stock tokenization so the real app prompts produced higher average tokens. once we run the tuned model with the quantized weights and adjusted kernel selection, we expect p95 to drop by ~20% in our sim, but that's an estimate
03:55 Tom Reynolds: is there a way to run a dedicated mini-cluster for a day to compare p95 under our traffic? we can open a credit line for that test if needed
04:05 Laura Kim: yes we can spin a short lived dedicated pool for a day as a paid bench. Miguel, can you scope the cost and expected improvement?
04:12 Miguel Santos: i'll scope today's numbers and put a cost estimate in the bench doc; i'll also include recommended batch/windows and TTL settings. expect an email with details by thursday
04:25 Sara Lee: regarding networking, we tried the VPC peering test and the tunnel works but there's intermittent packet drops when crossing regions — probably MTU or a path MTU issue
04:38 Laura Kim: ok that's useful — if you can capture a traceroute and the times when drops occur, our infra team can correlate. also region selection matters, we recommended same-region private during pilot to avoid cross-region tail latency
04:55 Aisha Khan: what's the expected timeline then for the private deep dive? we prefer next week if possible
05:03 Laura Kim: propose Tue 2026-03-03 for deep dive with security and infra, 60 minutes, we'll include a demo of KMS flow and network diagrams
05:12 Kevin O'Malley: that works tentatively, i'll confirm after i check calendar
05:20 Tom Reynolds: one open question on data retention — how long does Redwood keep logs by default, and can we configure a shorter retention for our pilot? we need 30-day retention max per policy
05:33 Priya Patel: default retention is 90 days for the hosted plan, but for dedicated/private we can set retention to 30 days and export audit logs to your SIEM. We'll add that to the onboarding runbook
05:48 Laura Kim: action recap — Miguel runs benchmark, Kevin sends KMS contact and network CIDRs, Laura sends SOC2/ISO and onboarding checklist, tom sends prompt set. we aim to close the network access and SSO by friday
06:05 Tom Reynolds: sounds good. minor transcription note — you might see 'Redwood Dedicated' mis-typed in notes, it's fine
06:12 Laura Kim: any other blockers?
06:15 Sara Lee: just the firewall and MTU checks, otherwise good
06:21 Aisha Khan: no blockers from product other than timeline confirmation
06:25 Laura Kim: perfect, we'll follow up with the docs and bench results. thanks everyone
06:30 Meeting end
